source.title: Sharpness of Minima in Deep Matrix Factorization: Exact Expressions

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices and experiments.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests gradient-descent stability near minima in deep matrix factorization with squared-error loss, a related but narrower setting than V5’s claims about training wide networks above the stability limit.
record.gate_note: The study’s results concern escape from an already constructed minimizer, not training from random initialization to fit a classification benchmark. It reports no CIFAR classification error, random-label fitting, or comparisons of width, initialization, normalization, or shortcuts.
record.test_reason: The study reports actual loss excursions and subsequent convergence above a local GD stability threshold in deep matrix factorization, equivalent to a restricted deep linear network setting. These results bear on V5's catapult component, although they do not establish curvature reduction or edge-of-stability training.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is accurate but incomplete. The authors derive exact minimum-sharpness expressions, characterize flatness, show that flat minima need not be balanced, and empirically demonstrate local GD escape above 2/λmax. They report a loss catapult followed by convergence to another minimum, while emphasizing limitations of quadratic local stability analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use full-batch GD on squared-error deep matrix factorization, initialized extremely close to a constructed minimizer and with step sizes set relative to its Hessian. They do not use the wide-network training recipe described in V5.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported escape/convergence outcome depends on whether the step size is above or at/below 2/λmax. Experiments vary depth, factor dimensions, initialization distance, and step size, but most curve outcomes are figure-only.

fits_no_version.finding: Exact maximum-Hessian-eigenvalue formulas and characterizations of flat minima, including counterexamples to balancedness claims.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In interpolating deep matrix factorization, minimum sharpness admits an exact expression, and Hessian-flat minima need not be balanced.

record.problems: The experiment initializes near known minimizers rather than from random initialization. It uses synthetic matrix-factorization targets and has no reported controls or uncertainty estimates. Most per-setting training-error and distance curves are figure-only; the text describes the threshold outcome generally.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification fitting, random labels, model-size effects, early stopping and regularization.
ReLU teacher-student spurious-minimum frequencies and the effect of excess student width.
Depth degradation in convolutional networks, identity shortcuts, deep tanh initialization and Fixup.
Comparative initialization effects on signal propagation, training speed and trainable depth.

Curvature reduction during recovery; the initial linearized threshold in ordinary training away from a constructed minimizer; sustained edge-of-stability sharpness trajectories; and divergence from initially subthreshold runs. Very-large-rate divergence is mentioned but not documented by an experimental row.
Batch normalization comparisons and normalization-free Fixup training.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any version. The specialized initialization defines the tested setting; unmeasured curvature and other training regimes do not themselves justify limits_scope. The supplied figure text preserves legends and axes but not readable curve paths, so no per-curve numerical outcomes are inferred for Figures 2–5.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels; model size, early stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima frequency, and excess student width.
Depth effects on classification training error in plain versus residual convolutional networks; special initializations and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.

The study uses deep matrix factorization, not wide neural networks; it initializes extremely close to a known minimizer rather than from random initialization. It does not test larger-than-reported learning rates that diverge or report recovery to low loss after a catapult in the same setting.
Batch normalization’s effect on speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training of residual networks.

rows.subject: depth-3 matrix factorization of a random 10 × 20 matrix
rows.operation_detail: GD initialized within 10−12 of a constructed minimizer along the maximum-Hessian-eigenvalue eigenvector
rows.measure: normalized squared distance from the minimizer and normalized training error over iterations
rows.value: η ≤ 2/λmax: GD converges to the minimizer; the plotted curve is figure only.
rows.note: The stated threshold rule classifies this equality case as convergence, not escape.
rows.check: This is a threshold control: absence of escape at η = 2/λmax does not challenge recovery above the threshold. The baseline is the constructed zero-loss minimizer and its initial perturbation.

rows.subject: depth-3 matrix factorization of a random 10 × 20 matrix
rows.operation_detail: GD initialized within 10−12 of a constructed minimizer along the maximum-Hessian-eigenvalue eigenvector
rows.measure: normalized squared distance from the minimizer and normalized training error over iterations
rows.value: For η > 2/λmax, GD escapes from the minimum; after escape it eventually converges to another minimum unless the step size is very large. Curves are figure only.
rows.note: Escape is reported, but the version’s recovery to low training loss after a catapult is not established for these runs.
rows.check: Section 6 explicitly reports a training-loss catapult followed by convergence to another minimum. Since all global minima in this setting interpolate, the record understates the textual evidence for recovery. Curvature reduction during the trajectory is not measured.
